                    ### Question
                    A 28-year-old pregnant female presents for a prenatal check-up at 20 weeks gestation, which includes routine screening ultrasound. Fetal ultrasound demonstrates bilateral multicystic dysplastic kidneys. Her pregnancy has been complicated by persistent oligohydramnios. The child requires significant pulmonary support upon delivery. Which of the following clinical findings is most likely present in this child as a result of these abnormalities?

                    ### Options
                    opa. Urachal fistula
opb. Esophageal atresia
opc. Spina bifida occulta
opd. Clubbed feet
ope. Macrosomia

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
Bilateral multicystic dysplastic kidneys lead to impaired renal function, which results in decreased amniotic fluid production and persistent oligohydramnios. This condition is associated with pulmonary hypoplasia due to limited lung development from reduced amniotic fluid. The oligohydramnios can also cause fetal compression, increasing the risk of musculoskeletal deformities, including clubbed feet. Therefore, the most likely clinical finding in this child, as a result of these abnormalities, is clubbed feet. The evidence paths support the link between oligohydramnios and musculoskeletal deformities, confirming the association with clubbed feet.
